title: LLaVA-ReID: Selective Multi-image Questioner for Interactive Person Re-Identification
authors: Yiding Lu, Mouxing Yang, Dezhong Peng, Peng Hu, Yijie Lin, Xi Peng
summary: Introduces interactive person re-identification, where a vision-language model asks targeted questions to refine an incomplete description. Selective multi-image context and informative question supervision help distinguish visually similar candidates over multiple rounds of dialogue.
image_alt: Comparison of text-based and interactive person re-identification, extracted from the official LLaVA-ReID poster

title: Visual Abstraction: A Plug-and-Play Approach for Text-Visual Retrieval
authors: Guofeng Ding, Yiding Lu, Peng Hu, Mouxing Yang, Yijie Lin, Xi Peng
summary: Improves text-to-image and text-to-video retrieval at test time by converting visual content into semantic descriptions. Query-guided question answering captures the level of detail a user needs, providing a plug-and-play enhancement to existing retrieval systems.
image_alt: Visual abstraction example showing query-specific attention to details in a snowy street scene

title: Decoupled Contrastive Multi-View Clustering with High-Order Random Walks
authors: Yiding Lu, Yijie Lin, Mouxing Yang, Dezhong Peng, Peng Hu, Xi Peng
summary: DIVIDE uses high-order random walks to identify misleading positive and negative pairs beyond local neighborhoods. Decoupled contrastive objectives preserve view-specific information while learning cross-view consistency, supporting clustering with complete or missing views.
image_alt: DIVIDE architecture with decoupled multi-view contrastive learning and random-walk pair correction

title: A Survey on Deep Clustering: From the Prior Perspective
authors: Yiding Lu*, Haobin Li*, Yunfan Li, Yijie Lin, Xi Peng
summary: Organizes deep clustering around six types of prior knowledge, connecting data structure, distribution assumptions, invariance, and external knowledge. The survey includes a five-dataset benchmark and examines how these priors shape representation learning and clustering.
image_alt: Six deep clustering priors: structure, distribution, augmentation invariance, neighborhood consistency, pseudo labels, and external knowledge

title: Semantic Invariant Multi-View Clustering With Fully Incomplete Information
authors: Pengxin Zeng, Mouxing Yang, Yiding Lu, Changqing Zhang, Peng Hu, Xi Peng
summary: SMILE learns shared semantics across views without requiring paired samples. Semantic invariance supports clustering, cross-view realignment, and missing-data recovery even when correspondences and observations are fully incomplete.
image_alt: SMILE framework for learning semantic invariance from incomplete multi-view data
